title: Semi-Quantum Cryptography with Certified Deletion
abstract: Certified deletion allows a client to upload encrypted data to a server as a quantum state, then later request that the server delete their data and detect whether the server complies. If verification passes, then the data on the server will remain hidden even if the decryption key is later leaked. In publicly verifiable certified deletion, the verification key is published so that anyone may check for deletion compliance.   In this work, we give a general compiler to publicly verifiable certified deletion that allows the client to initially upload the *quantum* ciphertext using purely *classical* communication, assuming the post-quantum hardness of LWE in the plain model. Our approach can be applied to a wide variety of primitives, including commitments and public-key, attribute-based, identity-based, and fully-homomorphic encryption.   Moreover, our constructions allow the client to classically manage the encrypted data beyond just verifying its deletion. The classical client may non-destructively audit the ciphertext via a Proof of No Intrusion to check whether it has been leaked to a third party. The classical client may also retrieve the data while simultaneously verifying its deletion from the server. Thus, they do not have to choose between retrieving the data and protecting it against future key leakage.   As our core technical contribution, we give a classical-communication protocol and simulation technique that allows adapting purification-based security arguments for BB84-style states which are prepared through classical interaction. It makes the required purification available in a hybrid experiment, despite the classical transcript uniquely determining the prepared state in a real execution.
summary: This work presents a general compiler for achieving publicly verifiable certified deletion in quantum cryptography, allowing quantum ciphertexts to be uploaded using only classical communication. It extends these capabilities to include non-destructive auditing (PoNI) and simultaneous data retrieval while ensuring deletion. The research is significant for building practical, robust quantum cryptographic primitives based on established hardness assumptions.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of creating a general compiler for publicly verifiable certified deletion in quantum cryptography, enabling the initial upload of quantum ciphertexts using only classical communication.
main_result: The authors provide a compiler assuming the post-quantum hardness of LWE, allowing for certified deletion, non-destructive auditing (PoNI), and simultaneous data retrieval/deletion protocols.
method: The core method involves developing a classical-communication protocol and simulation technique to adapt purification-based security arguments for BB84-style states prepared through classical interaction.
model_or_system: The model involves quantum states (specifically BB84-style states) representing quantum ciphertexts stored on a quantum server, secured by assumptions on the hardness of LWE.
key_observables: Certified deletion compliance, Proof of No Intrusion (PoNI) success, and the ability to verify deletion while retrieving data.
important_parameters: The security relies on the post-quantum hardness of LWE in the plain model.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the post-quantum hardness of LWE, and the technical contribution addresses the difficulty of applying purification arguments when the classical transcript uniquely determines the prepared state.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general compiler for certified deletion (Theorem 1) to detailing the specific mechanisms for PoNIs and the interactive classical protocol for simultaneous retrieval and deletion (Dec-Del).
why_interesting: While focused on classical communication and LWE, the underlying techniques for state preparation, verification, and security proofs are highly relevant to understanding the practical limits and security guarantees of quantum information protocols.
